content: The TAS2R9, also known as Taste Receptor Type 2 Member 9, is a protein encoded by the TAS2R9 gene in humans. This protein is part of the family of candidate taste receptors, which belong to the G-protein-coupled receptor superfamily. These receptors are specifically expressed in the taste receptor cells located in the epithelial tissues of the tongue and palate. The TAS2R9 protein and its related receptors are organized in clusters within the genome. These clusters are genetically linked to loci that influence the perception of bitterness in both mice and humans. Functional expression studies have demonstrated that these receptors respond to bitter-tasting compounds, known as bitter tastants. The TAS2R9 gene is located within the taste receptor gene cluster on chromosome 12p13. Variations, or polymorphisms, in this gene have been associated with differences in the perceived bitterness of the artificial sweetener acesulfame potassium.
